content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Org 'apexion' exceeding normal QPS (observed 18k sustained, baseline 2.1k). Error rate climbing to 5% for gen endpoints. Auto-throttle engaged. Paging on-call.

arjun: Paging in — oncall here. seeing spikes in both gen and embeddings. latency 95p up to 2.4s.

tess: confirmed in dashboards, spike started ~5m ago after a large batch job from apexion. Likely a customer side batch.

maria: marking customer impact: partial (some requests hit 429/504). Customer support case 48722 opened.

ops-annie: recommending immediate emergency mitigation: scope to org-level rate adjustment + temporary quota bump to avoid user-facing 5xxs? prefer rate-shape over global throttle.

arjun: agree. plan: 1) short-term org-level soft-qps cap to prevent node eviction, 2) enable org burst window + queue depth, 3) notify account team.

ryan: I can run the org-adjust CLI. will do a conservative bump then monitor.

arjun: do it behind a canary: route 10% of apexion traffic to dedicated burst pool first. if stable, expand.

ryan: running command now:
```
# grant apexion temporary burst capacity + soft cap
redwoodctl org update --org apexion --qps-burst 10000 --soft-cap 6000 --duration 30m --reason "emergency apexion spike 230912"
```

incident-bot: Command accepted and queued: job_id=job-9a7b.

ryan: applied canary routing rule (10% to burst pool). watching metrics.

maria: pinged AM and support, they acknowledged and will inform the customer ops.

ops-annie: noticed a concurrent increase in kv-cache misses for large prefixes from apexion. caching policies adjusted to avoid eviction thrash.

arjun: good. also toggle lightweight response sampling off for apexion to reduce compute cost for non-critical requests.

ryan: expanding to 50% after 2m stable.

incident-bot: telemetry: after 4m, error rate down to 1.2%, 95p latency 720ms. capacity headroom regained.

arjun: setting a temporary org-level hard cap at 12k QPS if we see node pressure again. Documenting decisions.

maria: support updated with rollback plan and ETA. Customer is likely running an internal migration, may hit again.

ryan: extending burst duration to 90m to cover customer window. command:
```
redwoodctl org update --org apexion --duration 90m --qps-burst 10000 --soft-cap 6000 --note "extend burst while customer migration completes"
```

ops-annie: note for ops: if nodes approach 85% GPU mem or 90% load, we should flip to org hard-cap 12k and fail-fast non-critical routes.

arjun: handoff: i'll be oncall for 30m then hand to @sre-rotation. leaving runbook steps in the thread. please escalate if we get sustained >12k.

sre-rotation: acknowledged, will monitor and take over at :50.

maria: action items: 1) support to confirm with customer that migration is in progress and ETA; 2) biz-ops to review billing for burst; 3) eng-sre to capture metrics and create post-incident ticket if regression.

arjun: adding temporary tag to org config so billing reflects emergency burst: `billing.note = \"emergency burst 230912 apexion\"`.

ryan: metrics look stable. will keep canary at 50% for now.

incident-bot: auto-reminder scheduled: in 60m re-evaluate and auto-expire burst if not extended.

maria: leaving a follow-up with customer team to get confirmation.

arjun: thanks all. documenting for postmortem. moving to monitoring-only; ping here if anything flips. :white_check_mark:

sre-rotation: taking over monitoring. will escalate to eng-oncall if latency trends back upward.

maria: closing support loop once customer confirms completion.

incident-bot: thread archived when last_message_ts surpasses 2309124120.
